about: A demo run, replayed from a live gpt-6-luna run (1015-130817-df98) at about 25x speed. The planner's question and every agent's edits and reports are that run's; in the live run the owner tried all six model families, and here you choose. The tests, checks and budget caps run for real on a fresh copy of repo/. Code identical to the live run's gets the score already measured for it, from scores.json (LUCIDITY_RESCORE=1 recomputes them all, about 10 minutes, mostly the SVM); any other code is scored for real. Agents were refused the held-out years; only Lucidity scored them. Returns, the Fama-French factors and momentum, and each industry's firm count, size and book-to-market are from Kenneth French's Data Library (49 industry portfolios, built from CRSP).
title: Stock returns

card.ask: Which industries beat the median next month? From past returns, factors, size and value.
card.why: Say 50% for every industry. Log loss charges 0.693 a row for that, so 0.693 means no skill. Plain regression on every column, factors included, does slightly worse.

blurb: A model predicts which of 49 industries will beat the median industry next month, from past returns, the Fama-French factors and momentum, and each industry's size, firm count and book-to-market. A coin flip scores 0.6931 log loss, so the goal is 0.6917. Six kinds of model are tried at once, one agent each, tuning on 2010-2016. Lucidity scores every attempt on 2017-2026, years the agents never see, and recommends the best, or tells you none of them works.
split: Trained on 1971-2009, tuned on 2010-2016, tested on 2017-2026. Agents never see the test years; only Lucidity scores them.

references.why: Say 50% for every row. Log loss charges 0.693 a row for that, so 0.693 means no skill at all.

about_repo: bundled industry-return model: 49 industries, monthly 1970-2026, Fama-French factors and industry size/value data, logistic regression, evals/score.py
commit_message: stockkit: last month + last year returns, logistic regression, 49 industries 1970-2026, Fama-French factors and industry size/value data, evals/score.py
goal: Get held-out log loss to 0.6917 or lower (a coin flip scores 0.6931) for predicting which industries beat the median next month, without accuracy dropping. Tune on the dev split. The repo has Fama-French factors, momentum, and each industry's firm count, size and book-to-market alongside the returns; use them. Ask the owner which model families to try (kNN, SVM, lasso or ridge logistic regression, random forest, boosted trees), then build each one in parallel and keep the best. Give each agent up to 4 rounds.

plan.summary: Run the requested family comparison on the dev split, with owner-selected model families implemented independently in parallel. Select the best dev log-loss candidate, preserve accuracy, and verify the held-out log-loss gate without tuning on held-out data.

nodes.title: Implement and compare owner-selected model families
nodes.prompt: For each family selected by the owner, independently implement a candidate in stockkit/model.py or an isolated model module, using the existing evaluation interface. Use dev split only for feature/model tuning; leverage available Fama-French factors, momentum, and industry firm count, size, and book-to-market where available, preserving the existing no-lookahead contract. Each candidate must be suitable for combining by the project owner, and document its dev score and accuracy; do not inspect or tune against heldout results.
strategies: kNN. Implement a leakage-safe sklearn kNN classifier with a dev-tuned neighbor count, distance weighting, and feature scaling; calibrate probabilities using dev only.
SVM. Implement an SVM candidate using standardized features and dev-tuned linear or RBF kernel settings; ensure probabilities are calibrated and assessed on dev only.

Lasso logistic regression. Implement logistic regression with L1 regularization and standardized features; tune regularization on dev, include available Fama-French factors and industry count/size/book-to-market features.

Ridge logistic regression. Implement logistic regression with L2 regularization and standardized features; tune regularization on dev, include available Fama-French factors and industry count/size/book-to-market features.
Random forest. Implement a random forest with dev-tuned tree depth, leaf size, and feature sampling; use only temporally valid features and assess probability loss on dev.
Boosted trees. Implement a boosted-tree classifier with conservative dev-tuned depth, learning rate, and iteration count; use temporal features only and assess log loss and accuracy on dev.

questions.question: Which model families should agents try? Select one or more; each selected family will be implemented and tuned on dev in parallel.

options.label: kNN
options.note: Can exploit similarity between industry-month feature profiles after appropriate scaling.
options.approach: Implement a leakage-safe sklearn kNN classifier with a dev-tuned neighbor count, distance weighting, and feature scaling; calibrate probabilities using dev only.

options.label: SVM
options.note: A nonlinear margin classifier can model interactions, with probability calibration needed.
options.approach: Implement an SVM candidate using standardized features and dev-tuned linear or RBF kernel settings; ensure probabilities are calibrated and assessed on dev only.

options.label: Lasso logistic regression
options.note: Sparse regularization can select useful signals from engineered momentum and cross-industry attributes.
options.approach: Implement logistic regression with L1 regularization and standardized features; tune regularization on dev, include available Fama-French factors and industry count/size/book-to-market features.

options.label: Ridge logistic regression
options.note: A stable regularized linear baseline is well suited to correlated financial predictors.
options.approach: Implement logistic regression with L2 regularization and standardized features; tune regularization on dev, include available Fama-French factors and industry count/size/book-to-market features.

options.label: Random forest
options.note: Can capture nonlinear interactions but may produce poorly calibrated probabilities on this small panel.
options.approach: Implement a random forest with dev-tuned tree depth, leaf size, and feature sampling; use only temporally valid features and assess probability loss on dev.

options.label: Boosted trees
options.note: Boosting may capture nonlinearities and can provide strong probability forecasts when regularized.
options.approach: Implement a boosted-tree classifier with conservative dev-tuned depth, learning rate, and iteration count; use temporal features only and assess log loss and accuracy on dev.

Tests pass, but the log-loss threshold is not demonstrated: held-out scoring was refused, and the dev score is above 0.6917.
